source_pages: printed p.230 / PDF 232, verified against a 170-dpi render 2026-08-23
family_note: NO family-level keys. THE FAMILY IS Wall H.36 AND THE SECTION IS 'Wall units H. 72', and that is not a mistake - it is the whole point of this file. printed p.230 prints this position inside the H.72 section, but its elevation is dimensioned 36, not 72. THE PRINTED DIMENSION OUTRANKS THE DECODED LETTER: PE reads H.72 in code_grammar.wall_units, and here it does not. The letter is a lookup for the SECTION, not a guarantee about the row. Height and mounting therefore come from wall_h36.json, which owns Wall H.36, and this file states none of its own.
extraction_note: One position, one code. Held in its own file rather than inside wall_h72.json because that file declares height_mm 720 for its family, and PE0696 is 360 - putting it there would have made the registry state a height the page contradicts.

wall_microwave_niche.description: Wall unit with top-hung door - 1 top-hung door - 1 adaptable microwave oven niche
wall_microwave_niche.notes: THE NICHE IS THE POINT AND IT IS NOT AN APPLIANCE. 'Adaptable' means the opening takes a microwave the client buys - so this is a Cesar carcass with a hole in it, ordered from Cesar, and the machine that goes in it is nobody's line here. It is NOT object_class appliance_front: that class is a PANEL bolted to a machine, and this is a cabinet. The niche itself is interior and is not drawn - envelope-only, like every shelf and divider. Suffix 96 appears nowhere else in the wall chapter.

front_layout.note: One door covering the full front of a 360-tall box, hinged along its top edge. The niche sits below it and is interior.
